title: Transform origin
learningObjectives: Explain transform origin and apply it in an accessible responsive interface.

understand.concept: transform-origin sets the point around which a transform is applied. It accepts positions such as center, top left, or percentages and lengths. The default origin for many HTML elements is the centre of the transform box.
understand.whyItMatters: Changing the origin can make the same rotation or scale look very different. Use it intentionally for interactive and decorative effects, and avoid unexpected movement that affects usability.
understand.analogy: A transform origin is like choosing the pin around which a paper card rotates.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; transforms and animations follow the CSS rendering and timing model.

explain.narrative: The card rotates around its left-centre point rather than its centre.

examples.explanation: The card rotates around its left-centre point rather than its centre.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example demonstrating the relevant responsive or animation behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Change transform-origin to center, top left, and bottom right while keeping the same rotation.
practise.independentTask: Build a small example that demonstrates the concept. Check keyboard access and reduced-motion behaviour where relevant.
hints: Test more than one viewport size.
Keep essential information available without motion.
Use developer tools to inspect computed values.
